source: CBSE Updated Syllabus 2026-27 (Play Group, Nursery, LKG, UKG)
notes: Hindi is taught in Nursery orally and in UKG with writing. Both were removed by an earlier product decision and restored on request; Play Group and LKG never published a Hindi subject.
Age bands are the product's, not the PDF's: the Play Group PDF states 2.5-3.5 years; this manifest uses 2-3 to make the four bands contiguous.
This file is the curriculum TAXONOMY only. Activities and questions are authored per topic from these subtopics.

`easy_line` and `subtopic_easy` are the child-facing explanation of a topic and of each of its points, in the syllabus's own plain words. `note` stays the editorial note for a grown-up reading this file and is not a card.

The published topics are delivered as short levels of three things each — Colours as three levels, Animals as four, and so on — because a two-year-old meets one thing at a time and a level has to fit in one sitting. subjects.note: The published syllabus lists Capital Letters (A-Z) and Small Letters (a-z) as two separate units. They are delivered here as 13 levels of two letters, each teaching the big and the small form of the same letter together — Aa, not A now and a much later — because that is what a three-year-old is being asked to recognise. Every published subtopic survives inside the levels: identification, letter sounds, one object per letter, matching capital with small, and writing (capitals throughout, small letters a-j, as published). Inside a level a letter is explained on three cards - the pair, its sound and word, and how both forms are made - then drawn, said aloud, and matched twice: small letter back to its capital, and the pair to the picture it starts.

subjects.title: Hindi (Oral Introduction)
subjects.note: Oral only. The published syllabus says so in as many words — "Is saal Hindi likhna nahi hai" — so a Hindi level is meet it, find it, find its picture, say it, and there is no tracing step anywhere in this subject. Everything else follows Nursery English: one letter at a time, two per level, taught before it is asked, each level unlocking the next. The twelve swar are paired as a child hears them (अ आ, इ ई, उ ऊ, ए ऐ, ओ औ, अं अः); ऋ is not taught at this age and the syllabus's own examples stop at ई. Only क to ङ are introduced, as published.
